current_activity: Blackcock: attacks from the Wurm to the Juliana Canal; 7th Armoured Division leads on the left at 07:30
notes: Event date: 16 January 1945, 07:30 (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 242, 243). Event definition: Operation Blackcock: the front to be attacked by XII Corps runs from the river Wurm, just north of Geilenkirchen, to the Juliana Canal near Maeseyck on the Maas, in a triangle between the Roer and the Maas with its apex at Roermond; General Ritchie decides to start on the left with the 7th Armoured Division and then to follow with attacks by the 52nd Division in the centre and the 43rd Division on the right; delayed by thick fog, the attack begins at 07:30 on 16 January; the only roads of any standing radiate from Sittard to Geilenkirchen, Heinsberg and Roermond (pp. 242-243). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 242: "The front to be attacked by XII Corps ran from the river Wurm, just north of Geilenkirchen, to the Juliana Canal near Maeseyck on the river Maas"; p. 243: "XII Corps commander (General Ritchie) decided to start his attack on the left with 7th Armoured Division and as it progressed to follow with attacks by 52nd Division in the centre and 43rd Division on the right"; "Delayed by thick fog, the attack began at 7.30 a.m. on January the 16th". Location: Sittard, Limburg (new place), on the roads that radiate across the corps front with a precision of 25 km. Location approximate: the point is Sittard, the road centre in the middle of the front named (the Wurm at Geilenkirchen to the Juliana Canal near Maeseyck, about 35 km); the corps headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis gives the corps front from the Wurm near Geilenkirchen to the Juliana Canal near Maeseyck and names Sittard as the road centre of the area (pp. 242-243). Commander: General Ritchie, the XII Corps commander who decided the plan of attack (Ellis, vol. II, p. 243).

current_activity: Plunder: the corps assaults the Rhine from Xanten to Wesel; the Commandos cross at 22:00, the 15th Division at 02:00
notes: Event date: the night of 23-24 March 1945 (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 285, 289). Event definition: Twenty-First Army Group's order of battle for the Rhine crossing puts in XII Corps (Assault) the 7th Armoured Division, the 15th, 52nd and 53rd Divisions, the 4th and 34th Armoured Brigades and the 1st Commando Brigade (p. 285, note); on the night of 23 March, an hour after the 51st Division's assault at 21:00, the 1st Commando Brigade of XII Corps crosses about two miles downstream of Wesel and the whole brigade is in Wesel by first light after Bomber Command's raid; at 02:00 on 24 March the XII Corps assault by the 15th (Scottish) Division opposite Xanten begins (pp. 288-289). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 285: "XII Corps (Assault): 7th Armoured Division, 15th, 52nd and 53rd Divisions"; p. 289: "An hour after the 51st Division's assault the 1st Commando Brigade of XII Corps crossed about two miles downstream of Wesel"; "the XII Corps assault by the 15th (Scottish) Division opposite Xanten began". Location: Xanten, North Rhine-Westphalia (existing place PL0697), the middle of the corps assault front from Xanten to Wesel with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is Xanten, at the western end of the corps front (Wesel lies about 15 km to the east); the corps headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names the assault opposite Xanten and the Commando crossing downstream of Wesel (p. 289).
